# Ellen West

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)</sub>

## Appearance

Ellen is dark, stately, and massive, with black hair, thick black eyebrows, and clear, slaty blue eyes. She has a stern, forbidding appearance that can look quite handsome in her black-browed style. She possesses a pleasant, deep, mellow voice with a hint of masculinity.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c22 P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008)_

## Personality

Despite her stern exterior, Ellen is very jolly, possesses a hearty laugh, and enjoys humour and good jokes. She is intelligent, well-read, highly interested in world politics, and demonstrates an almost masculine understanding that makes her pleasant to talk with. Although she has a history of being moody during times of grief, she is generally spunky, spirited, and stands up for herself.

_Sources: [v5 c12 P18](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0018), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P17](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0017), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006)_

## History

Ellen grew up living with her sister Rosemary and their mother after her father and brother died. In her youth, she went about with Norman Douglas for two years before a quarrel caused them to separate, leading Norman to marry someone else out of pique. Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, Ellen sank into a deep period of intense grief and melancholy. During this time, she had Rosemary swear a solemn vow over the Bible that neither of them would ever marry and that they would always live together. Over the years, she and Rosemary kept close to home, maintaining their household on the hill. Years later, Norman Douglas saw her at church and fell in love with her again, prompting him to pursue her and ultimately leading to their arrangement to marry.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P17](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0017), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Quotes

> The day never goes by for men and nations to make asses of themselves and take to the fists. The millenniun isn’t that near, Mr. Meredith, and you don’t think it is any more than I do. As for this Kaiser, mark my words, he is going to make a heap of trouble—and Miss Ellen prodded her book emphatically with her long finger. Yes, if he isn’t nipped in the bud he’s going to make trouble. We’ll live to see it—you and I will live to see it, Mr. Meredith. And who is going to nip him? England should, but she won’t. Who is going to nip him? Tell me that, Mr. Meredith.  <sub>[v5 c13 P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029)</sub>
